items.title: 12.1.2 Meaning of the Phrase "x approaches infinity" (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein terms chhote hote ja rahe the. Aaj bilkul ulti kahani hai: terms bare hote jaate hain, itne bare ke koi hadd (limit) hi nahin rehti. Is ko kehte hain "x approaches infinity".
Kitab kehti hai: farz karein sequence \(x_{n} = 10^{n}\) yeh values leta hai: \(1, 10, 10^{2}, 10^{3}, \ldots, 10^{n}, \ldots\)

Saaf zahir hai ke jaise jaise \(n\) barhta hai, sequence \(x_{n}\) bara aur bara hota jata hai, aur \(n\) ko kaafi bara le kar hum use jitna chahein bara bana sakte hain. Sequence ke is kabhi na rukne wale izafe (unending increase) ko "\(x_{n} \to \infty\)" likhte hain aur parhte hain "\(x_{n}\) approaches infinity" ya "\(x_{n}\) tends to infinity" as \(n \to \infty\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehli value \(1\) hai, jo \(10^{0}\) hai. Is liye yahan \(n\) ki values \(0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\) hain. Yeh chhoti si baat hai lekin dhyan rakhiye.
"Jitna chahein bara" ka matlab: aap koi bhi bara number bata dein, ek term ke baad saare terms us se bhi bare honge. Misal: humein chahiye \(x_{n} > 1{,}000{,}000 = 10^{6}\). Yani \(10^{n} > 10^{6}\), yani \(n > 6\).
Kyun: base \(10\) ek se bara hai, is liye jitni bari power, utna bara number; powers ka muqabla karna hi kaafi hai.
To 7vi power se aage har term das lakh (one million) se bara hai. Ek arab (\(10^{9}\)) chahiye to \(n > 9\) le lein. Aap jitna bhi bara number bolein, \(n\) mil jayega.

blocks.caption: Hamari table (kitab mein nahin): n barhne ke saath x_n = 10^n ke terms kisi hadd ke baghair barhte jaate hain.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text:
Infinity (\(\infty\)) koi number nahin hai. Is ko jama, tafreeq (subtract) ya substitute nahin kiya ja sakta jaise numbers ko karte hain. \(x_{n} \to \infty\) bas ek chhota tareeqa hai yeh kehne ka ke "\(x_{n}\) har hadd se aage nikal jata hai".
Socho, sab se bara number kaun sa hai? Jo bhi number aap bolein, us mein 1 jama kar dein to us se bara number mil jata hai. Is liye koi "sab se bara number" hota hi nahin, aur \(\infty\) is be-hadd barhne ka naam hai, kisi number ka nahin.
Isi tarah \(x \to -\infty\) ka matlab hai \(x\) negative hai aur us ka size barhta ja raha hai, jaise \(-10, -100, -1000, \ldots\) Yeh aap 12.2.3 mein dekhenge.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Sequence \(x_{n} = 2^{n}\) (\(n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\)) kya infinity ki taraf jata hai? Kitne terms ke baad yeh 1000 se bara ho jata hai?
Jawab: haan, \(2, 4, 8, 16, \ldots\) har hadd se aage nikal jata hai. \(2^{9} = 512\) aur \(2^{10} = 1024\), is liye 10ve term se aage har term 1000 se bara hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Shatranj (chess) ki mashhoor kahani yaad karein: pehle khaane mein gandum ka ek daana, doosre mein do, teesre mein chaar, har khaane mein pichhle ka dugna. Sirf 64 khaanon mein daanon ki tadaad itni bari ho jaati hai ke poori duniya ki gandum kam par jaaye. Dugna ya das guna hote rehne wali sequence isi tarah infinity ki taraf daurti hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Dono jumlon ka muqabla yaad rakhiye: \(x_{n} \to 0\) (12.1.1) ka matlab terms jitna chahein chhote (zero ke qareeb), aur \(x_{n} \to \infty\) ka matlab terms jitna chahein bare. Dono mein \(n \to \infty\) hai. Aur in mein rishta bhi hai: agar \(x_{n} = 10^{n} \to \infty\) to \(\frac{1}{x_{n}} = \frac{1}{10^{n}} \to 0\). Bara number ulta karo to chhota ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(x_{n} = 10^{n}\) se \(1, 10, 100, 1000, \ldots\) milte hain: terms be-inteha barhte hain.
2. \(n\) kaafi bara lein to terms kisi bhi chune hue number se bare ho jaate hain.
3. Is ko likhte hain \(x_{n} \to \infty\) as \(n \to \infty\), aur parhte hain "\(x_{n}\) approaches (tends to) infinity".
4. \(\infty\) be-hadd izafe ka nishan hai, koi real number nahin.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\infty\) ko number samajh lena, jaise jawab mein \(10^{\infty}\) likhna ya \(\infty - \infty = 0\) kehna. In ka koi matlab nahin.
2. Yeh samajhna ke sirf "bara hota ja raha hai" kaafi hai. Sequence \(1 - \frac{1}{n}\) ke terms (\(0, 0.5, 0.67, 0.75, \ldots\)) bare hote jaate hain lekin kabhi \(1\) se aage nahin jaate; yeh infinity ki taraf nahin jata, \(1\) ki taraf jata hai. Infinity ki taraf jaane ke liye har hadd se aage nikalna zaroori hai.
